objective: Architectural sign-off on the grove-explore binary: a dedicated single-tool stdio MCP server with a hard startup health gate that exits non-zero before the loop rather than falling back.
key_changes: Fits the stack unchanged: second [[bin]] reuses the hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 surface, same SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS, clap/serde, no new deps.
Startup health gate (config load -> explore deser -> health_probe, each process::exit(1) before serve_explore) enforces 'never fall back'; test asserts non-zero exit + empty stdout.
Config source respects ADR 0002: GroveConfig::load -> grove_cfg.explore -> ExploreConfig with no config-file move (Stage 3 deferred by design).
In-process explorer call (run_explore_reporting) with no MCP hop; mid-session ProviderDown returns isError:true identical to mcp.rs; grove binary behaviour unchanged.
Independent code-review and validation both green: 337 workspace tests pass, clippy --all-targets --workspace --locked -D warnings clean; AC1-AC7 all met.
Deployment: grove now emits a SECOND release artifact. npm/Homebrew/install-script/GH-Releases ship one binary; grove-explore packaging is T04/T06 but MUST land before any user-facing release.
Follow-up: T03 dedup clears ~130 LOC copied from mcp.rs (explore_tool_spec, protocol consts, ProviderDown arm); keep T02->T03 ordering tight.
